cf.title: Incorrect historic snapshot may be serialized to disk during fast-forwarding

input.subject: [BUG] Incorrect historic snapshot may be serialized to disk during fast-forwarding

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated with a reproducer in message #1, and message #10 reports an output plugin failure that v4 fixes. The one surviving objection, replication-ondisk-1, is a fixable level 2 point about snapshot files written before the fix and about back branches. A committer who knows the snapshot builder has to decide those two points.

brief.title: Mark NEW_CID transactions as catalog-changing during fast-forward decoding
brief.problem: During fast-forward decoding, heap2_decode() skips XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID, so a transaction that writes only NEW_CID records is not marked as catalog-changing. The serialized historic snapshot then lacks that XID, and a later decoding run at the same LSN builds a different snapshot. The case the thread shows is a write to a user_catalog_table, which matters for output plugins and extensions that scan such tables.
brief.proposed_design: heap2_decode() handles XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID also when fast-forwarding and marks the transaction as containing catalog changes. The other NEW_CID processing still runs only outside fast-forward. In fast-forward, the record no longer falls through to the XLOG_HEAP2_REWRITE case.
author_claims: Two decoding runs at the same LSN produce different historic snapshots, and the incorrect one from the fast-forward run is serialized to disk.
The bug breaks the snapshot builder design, which tracks all catalogs, even if it may be harmless in practice today.
An extension that scans a user_catalog_table with the incorrect snapshot gets wrong results.
The reviewer reproduced an output plugin catalog lookup failure without the patch and confirmed v4 fixes it.
Common DDL always writes XLOG_XACT_INVALIDATIONS too, so plain DDL does not hit the bug in the reviewer's tests.
brief.thread_state: Masahiko Sawada agreed with the analysis but asked for a real-world problem, ideally reproduced with DDL. Yuya Shinde reproduced a plugin failure with a user_catalog_table, found no DDL reproducer, and posted a test patch on top of v4; no committer has replied since.
unclear: Whether any core path or supported extension writes NEW_CID without invalidations, outside user_catalog_table writes.
What the snapbuild.c change in v4 does; the commit message covers only decode.c.
Whether the fix is meant for back branches, and which ones.
Whether already serialized wrong snapshots in pg_logical/snapshots need any cleanup after upgrade.
What the output plugin failure in the reviewer's reproduction looked like.
search_queries: logical decoding skip records fast forward

objections.title: Wrong snapshot files already on disk keep being reused after the fix
objections.failure_scenario: A user installs a minor release with the fix on a server where an earlier fast-forward run, such as pg_replication_slot_advance, wrote a snapshot file to pg_logical/snapshots without the NEW_CID transaction. A slot created or restarted at that LSN restores the file instead of rebuilding the snapshot. An output plugin that scans a user_catalog_table then reads the wrong rows, with no error to show it.
objections.argument: The patch changes how snapshots are built from now on, but message #1 shows the defect persists as a serialized file that a later run at the same LSN can read. CheckPointSnapBuild removes such files only once no slot needs them. The proposal does not say whether it targets back branches, or whether files written before the fix stay valid, need removal, or need a SNAPBUILD_VERSION bump. The commit message also does not say what the snapbuild.c change does, so a reviewer cannot tell whether the on-disk snapshot format changes.
objections.author_must_show: After a minor upgrade, can a snapshot file written by an unpatched fast-forward run still be restored, and if so, what removes or rejects it?

critic.reasoning: A slot that restarts decoding restores the serialized snapshot at its restart point, and the thread does not discuss files written before the fix or back branches. The exposure ends once slots advance and a checkpoint removes the files, so `fixable` is the right severity.

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the snapshot builder and logical decoding. Masahiko Sawada asked for a real-world problem earlier in the thread, and no committer has replied since the reproduction in message #10.
committability.liability: The owner signs for historic snapshot correctness on the fast-forward path, in every branch that gets the fix, and for the decision on snapshot files written before it.
committability.author_follow_up: The authors posted revisions up to v4 and moved the entry across CommitFests through 2026-08, so they appear to stay with it.

priority.reason: The fix is under 3 KiB in decode.c and snapbuild.c, adds no user-visible surface, and affects only output plugins and extensions that scan a user_catalog_table. It has been in 5 CommitFests, and no committer has answered the reproduction in message #10.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical decoding and replication of sequences, take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend logical decoding with a sequence callback, and extend built-in logical replication so publications can include sequences, so that a logical replica's sequences track the primary and do not produce duplicate values after failover. Sequence increments were decoded non-transactionally by default, and transactionally when the sequence's relfilenode was created or altered in an in-progress transaction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the 2024 'take 2' entry was withdrawn. They do show that an earlier committed version was reverted in April 2022. Review had found that non-transactional sequence changes could be discarded or hit an assertion before the decoding snapshot was consistent, and mixing transactional and non-transactional decoding caused snapshot, abort and streaming problems. The author judged that a fix would need an extensive redesign that was too late for that release cycle, and posted an alternative that WAL-logs sequence state at commit time.
matched_queries: logical decoding skip records fast forward
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The approach combining transactional and non-transactional behavior implemented by the patch clearly has issues, and it seems foolish to hope we'll find a simple fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
matched_queries: logical decoding skip records fast forward
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a hot standby. It adds a catalog-table flag to existing WAL records so the standby can detect snapshot conflicts with logical slots, and it drops conflicting slots, including when wal_level on the primary drops below logical.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn. The last messages show the patch set needing repeated rebases and its TAP tests failing intermittently: Rahila Syed reported 018_standby_logical_decoding_xmins.pl failures, and Alvaro Herrera found 019_standby_logical_decoding_conflicts.pl timing out after a rebase in March 2020. No later reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
Reverted commit(s): Standardize LSN formatting by zero padding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 2633dae2e48 standardized LSN formatting but mistakenly changed
the logical snapshot filename format in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() from
"%X-%X.snap" to "%08X-%08X.snap". Other code still used the original
"%X-%X.snap" format, causing the replication slot synchronization worker
to fail to find existing snapshot files and produce excessive log messages.

This commit restores the original "%X-%X.snap" format
in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() to resolve the issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip collecting decoded changes of already-aborted transactions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding checks CLOG when it first decodes a transaction and stops collecting decoded changes for transactions already known to be aborted, so large aborted transactions are not decoded again after a restart or lag. After Andres Freund's review, the revised patch checks transaction status only for large transactions at eviction time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The revised patch did not compile because `logical_replication_mode` was undeclared in `ReorderBufferCheckTXNAbort`. The author posted no new version after this report, so the CF manager returned the entry with feedback. Andres Freund's earlier concerns, misuse of TransactionIdDidAbort() and slow CLOG lookups, were addressed in the design but not decisive.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical decoding of two-phase transactions
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alvaro Herrera, Arseny Sher, Petr Jelinek
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets logical decoding decode a two-phase transaction at PREPARE TRANSACTION time, with output plugin callbacks for prepare, commit prepared and abort prepared. To handle a concurrent ROLLBACK PREPARED during decoding, it first used decode groups that blocked the abort, then later versions stopped decoding when catalog access saw the transaction aborted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed as Returned with feedback because no new patch version was posted after the January 2019 reviews. Those reviews reported open problems, among them that calling SnapBuildCommitTxn at PREPARE makes the catalog changes visible too early. Earlier, in July 2018, Robert Haas questioned whether blocking transaction aborts could work at all, and Andres Freund objected to a planned commit in April 2018.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: XLog size reductions: Reduced XLog record header size
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patchset makes the WAL record header variable-length, which shrinks it to 14-21 bytes, with about 4-5% less WAL estimated for pgbench. It varlength-encodes the record length, gives rmgrs their own info byte, includes the XID only when the record asks for it with XLOG_INCLUDE_XID, and adds an invalid rmgr ID 0 used to detect the end of WAL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after review. Michael Paquier objected to the opt-in XLOG_INCLUDE_XID interface and questioned the use of rmgr ID 0 as an end-of-WAL marker. Pavel Borisov then asked for benchmarks showing the gain was large enough, the benchmarking was still a todo, and a reminder from Andrey M. Borodin in April 2024 got no visible reply before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But at the second round, some doubt arises on whether this long
patchset indeed introduces enough performance gain?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved candidates do not cover this idea. Message #1 points to a related historic snapshot bug thread, but the thread says nothing about how it ended, so no earlier rejection reason applies here.

The patch changes only how fast-forward decoding treats XLOG_HEAP2_NEW_CID. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql feature or dump content, and it does not change what clients or output plugins are told to expect. Two points could not be checked without the code: whether the snapbuild.c change alters the serialized snapshot file format, and whether wrong snapshots already on disk survive a minor upgrade. The thread does not discuss either point.

Only one objection from this angle. The fix adds no WAL record, catalog change or wire protocol change, and touches only snapshot building. The one persistent effect is the serialized snapshot files covered above.

The patch adds no privilege, default or new exposure. It changes when fast-forward decoding marks a NEW_CID transaction as catalog-changing, so a serialized historic snapshot includes more XIDs, and the users who can create and advance slots stay the same. The patch has no security or privilege aspect.

The fix is a small bugfix in decode.c that lets fast-forward decoding of NEW_CID mark catalog changes, as non-fast-forward decoding already does; it adds no new mechanism, setting or API. The extra cost falls only on fast-forward runs that meet NEW_CID records and matches normal decoding. Not checked without code: what the snapbuild.c hunk in v4 changes. Committability: no committer has engaged since message #6, so the patch has no owner yet.

This is a bug fix inside heap2_decode() for fast-forward decoding. No existing feature, option, extension or external tool gives a correct serialized snapshot in this case, and the fix extends the existing NEW_CID handling without adding a second mechanism. Other angles may question demand and real-world impact (message #6).

This is a small correctness fix on the fast-forward path, and message #10 reproduces an output plugin catalog lookup failure through user_catalog_table, the case that option exists for. The thread has no field report, but that affects priority and backpatching rather than whether the fix is wanted, and non-users pay almost nothing.
